column1: What distinguishes size from capacity in a dynamic array?
column2: Size counts stored elements. Capacity counts allocated slots. Only indexes 0 through size - 1 contain elements.

column1: Why does a dynamic array support O(1) access by index?
column2: Elements occupy consecutive slots, so an index directly identifies a slot without scanning earlier elements.

column1: Why is inserting or deleting near the front of a dynamic array O(n)?
column2: The following elements must shift to preserve order and keep occupied slots consecutive.

column1: Why is append O(1) amortized when a dynamic array doubles its capacity?
column2: Resize copies form a geometric sum (4 + 8 + 16 + ...), totaling O(n) across n appends. One resizing append still costs O(n).

column1: You need an ordered sequence with frequent indexed access and additions at the end. Which structure fits?
column2: A dynamic array (Python list): O(1) indexed access and O(1) amortized append.
